name: Cutting garlic and onion
lead: Cutting garlic and onion is the practice of avoiding these foods to reduce body and breath odor. Garlic breath arises mainly from volatile sulfur compounds, especially allyl methyl sulfide (AMS), formed as allicin breaks down; AMS is the longest-lasting and can persist for up to two days.[1]

AMS is absorbed into the bloodstream and leaves the body through the lungs, kidneys and skin, which is why mouthwash and mints are described as not particularly effective.[1] Grokipedia says garlic and onion produce AMS that is exhaled and secreted in sweat.[2]

paras: A 2020 Scientific Reports study by Sato, Sekine and Kakumu measured diallyl disulfide and AMS emitted from human skin and tested the effect of eating grilled garlic.[3] A 2024 Applied Sciences paper by Hiramoto and colleagues examined whether ingesting food additives containing phenolic compounds and polyphenol oxidase can reduce garlic body odor.[3]

An Ohio State University study (2010) found milk reduced garlic breath, and another study identified raw lettuce, mint, parsley and apple-type foods among remedies, with raw foods working better because the degrading enzymes are heat-sensitive.[1]
Small human studies have measured garlic-derived compounds on skin and in breath, as above.[1][3] Studies of eliminating garlic and onion to improve social perception of body odor were not found.

timeline.event: Ohio State study finds milk reduces garlic breath.[1]
Sato et al. measure garlic-derived compounds from skin.[3]
Hiramoto et al. study polyphenol-based reduction of garlic body odor.[3]

card.summary: Garlic compounds are documented in breath and skin emissions; avoiding garlic and onion is a plausible odor lever, with limited direct trials.
card.note: Odor compounds persist up to about two days.

quick.overview:
Garlic and onion contain sulfur compounds that appear in breath and skin emissions for up to two days. Some people avoid them to reduce odor.

Research measures the compounds and some countermeasures but not avoidance for social outcomes.
quick.mechanism: Allicin breaks down into allyl methyl sulfide, absorbed into the blood and released via lungs, kidneys and skin.
quick.risks: No risks documented in the sources consulted.
